summary: New Bedford Harbor's Palmer Island Light: an 1849 stone tower, the 1938 hurricane that took the keeper's wife, and a 1999 solar relight on a city-owned island.

lens.where: Fifth-order Fresnel from 1856 (LighthouseFriends; USLHS); a fourth-order Fresnel by 1931 (LighthouseFriends); the current optic is a 250 mm solar light (USLHS)

structures.note: Rubble masonry, 24 ft (NRHP). The station record gives 7.0 m.
Keeper's dwelling destroyed in the 1938 hurricane (NRHP; LighthouseFriends).

Pyramidal wooden fog-bell tower, 31 May 1900; the NRHP says the 1900 tower was apparently destroyed by storms or removed about 1902, and a later bell tower stood by 1929; the 1966 fire may have destroyed that one.
Oil house built on the island in 1905 (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Island is designated for walking and passive recreation; fishing and shellfishing are prohibited (PCBs); cross at low tide by the sand spit. The lighthouse is open only by arrangement with the city (visitor guide).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends and USLHS: fifth-order Fresnel from 1856; the NRHP dates a lens replacement to 1857. Not resolved; both reported.
NRHP and the station record: automated 1941. LighthouseFriends: automated and made unattended in 1942. The story gives 1941 with the LighthouseFriends date noted.
The roster ends the stint in 1939; the 1938 hurricane and LighthouseFriends' two-year absence with pay explain the later end date.

The NRHP says the wife drowned 'while attempting to reach the light'; the Bulletin says she tried to launch a boat, then (later text) lost her life trying to help her husband; LighthouseFriends says she was trying to launch a rowboat. The story reports the Bulletin's account and notes the NRHP's wording.

The station record gives Fl W 4s (from its enc source). LighthouseFriends describes a white flash every seven and a half seconds after the 1999 relight. The story does not state the characteristic; the JSON carries LighthouseFriends' figure.
The NRHP gives $1951 as the masonry contract; LighthouseFriends gives the $3,500 appropriation and says the project came in $173 under budget. Not resolved.
Roster: Frank J. Ponte. LighthouseFriends: Franklin Ponte. Same stint.
The keeper's report (Bulletin 1938, PDF page 38) says he was removed to St. Luke's hospital; LighthouseFriends says Chelsea Marine Hospital under police escort. Not resolved; the story reports both.

The keeper's report (quoted in the Commissioner's letter, PDF page 38) puts Mrs. Small in the oil house, where he had told her to stay in the upper part. The Commissioner's own text on the same page, and a later Bulletin text (PDF page 39), put her in the tower. The story reports the disagreement and the three accounts of how she died.
NRHP narrative: Sara Small. LighthouseFriends and the visitor listing: Mabel. The story names her only as Mrs. Arthur A. Small in the storm account and gives both names.

NRHP: substitute keeper Martin Maloney, stationed at Bullock's light during the hurricane and still tending Palmer Island in August 1939. LighthouseFriends: Franklin Ponte filled in after Small, and Andrew Zuius was keeper at Bullocks Point in 1938. Not resolved.

LighthouseFriends: hurricane wall built 1963. NRHP: hurricane barrier built 1962-66. Visitor listing: completion of the hurricane barrier in 1966. Story gives LighthouseFriends' 1963 with the listing's 1966.

notes_for_editor: Roster matched by name and position (0.08 km). Key 1938 details come from the Lighthouse Service Bulletin's reprint of the Commissioner's letter and the keeper's report; the Bulletin's OCR interleaves columns on pages 38 and 39, so quotations are short and the page for the keeper's preparations and the 'remained at his post' passage is taken as page 38 (not confirmed on the page image). LighthouseFriends carries the most narrative detail (Small's words, the Chelsea hospital, the 1920s-1990s history) and is the only source for several items: the Rodman whale-oil trial, the 1885 bridge light request, the 1931 inspection, the Franklin Ponte name. The 1918-1923 Bulletin index cites a Faulkner 'rescue' at page 136; the narrative was not located, so the story uses the 1920 tow only. Caroline Stubbs: a Chronicling America search for her name at Palmer Island, 1861-1873, returned no pages. The city and Cape Cod Life pages are current visitor information; check before publishing access guidance. Wikipedia not used. Fact-check 2026-10-22: the 1938 Bulletin pages PDF 38 (printed 134) and PDF 39 (printed 135) were read as OCR and checked against the page images. Page 38 holds the Commissioner's letter (keeper helped his wife to the tower; she left the tower to launch a boat), the keeper's report quoted within it (she left the oil house; 'Keeper removed to St. Luke's hospital'), and the Commissioner's commendation. Page 39 holds the news note ('who had first taken refuge in the tower, lost her life in an attempt to go to the assistance of her husband'). The printed page numbers are read from the images. The NRHP narrative names the wife Sara Small and a substitute keeper Martin Maloney, neither in the USLHS or LighthouseFriends; the story reports both. Explore New Bedford is a visitor listing; its operator was not confirmed, so the story calls it a listing, not the city. The 1900 Board entry (fog bell, 31 May 1900) is on scan page 60 with the repairs list.
